title: Absence of sections supported on the total exceptional locus after two transforms
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme, $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal, $b:S_1=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(S)\to S$ its blowup, $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_{S_1}$ a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal, and $c:S_2=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}(S_1)\to S_1$ its blowup [def-pc-scheme], [pqf-def-coherent], [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Write $Z=V(\mathcal I)$, $Z_1=V(\mathcal J)$, and $E=b^{-1}Z$. For any morphism $f:X\to S$ and quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$, set $X_i=X\times_SS_i$, let $f_2:X_2\to S_2$ be the projection, let $\mathcal F_1$ be the module strict transform along $b$, and let $\mathcal F_2$ be the module strict transform of $\mathcal F_1$ along $c$ [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-trf-module-strict-transform]. Then $\mathcal F_2$ has no nonzero local sections supported on $f_2^{-1}c^{-1}(|Z_1|\cup|E|)$: for every open $W\subseteq X_2$, a section of $\mathcal F_2(W)$ restricting to zero on $W\setminus f_2^{-1}c^{-1}(|Z_1|\cup|E|)$ is zero. Moreover the equality of subsets
$$c^{-1}(|Z_1|\cup|E|)=(bc)^{-1}(|Z|\cup b(|Z_1|))$$
holds on $S_2$.

proof.text: Put f₁ = pullback.snd f I.blowupMap, F₁ = moduleStrictTransform f I F, and D = I.comap I.blowupMap. Principalization makes D invertible. The first strict-transform properties give quasi-coherence of F₁ and sectionwise injectivity of its restriction unit away from f₁⁻¹D. Sectionwise injectivity is equivalent to this unit being a monomorphism. The complement open agrees with moduleStrictTransformOpen f I by the support-comap formula.

proof.text: Multiplication by the invertible ideal D gives an isomorphism φ : Bl_(JD)(S₁) ≅ Bl_J(S₁) over S₁. Apply the different-centres kernel comparison to f₁, J, D, φ and F₁, using the monomorphism from step 1. This identifies the kernels of restriction of the common ambient module P to the usual centre complement and to the transported product-centre complement. The latter open is exactly (pullback.snd f₁ J.blowupMap ≫ J.blowupMap)⁻¹(J.support.compl ∩ D.support.compl), by the projection equation for the induced fibre-product isomorphism and V(JD)=V(J)∪V(D).

proof.text: An equality of kernel subobjects identifies the cokernels of their inclusions. Thus F₂ before fibre-product reassociation is isomorphic to the coimage of restriction of P to the product-centre complement V. In an abelian category the coimage has a monomorphism to j_*j^*P. The restriction adjunction has invertible counit, so its unit on j_*j^*P is invertible. Naturality of the unit then shows its unit on the coimage, and hence on F₂, is mono: its composite with the induced map is the composite of two monomorphisms. This proves saturation without constructing the product-centre strict transform or proving its finite type.

proof.text: Transport the resulting unit monomorphism along the inverse fibre-product pasting isomorphism a. Tensor pullback along an open immersion is naturally isomorphic to restriction, by uniqueness of left adjoints to pushforward. Restriction carries sectionwise injectivity over V to sectionwise injectivity over a⁻¹V: the image of W∩a⁻¹V is a(W)∩V, and restriction maps commute. The pasting projection identity identifies a⁻¹V with moduleIteratedStrictTransformOpen. Evaluation preserves monomorphisms, giving the asserted implication for every W and section s.

source.place: Tag 080I, lemma-strict-transform-composition-blowups, final proof paragraph and its equality of support sets; Tag 080H, lemma-strict-transform-different-centers (2); Tag 02OS, lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor.

proof.text: For the set equality, the forward inclusion sends a point of V(J) to its image under b, and a point over V(I) to V(I). Conversely, if b(c(t)) lies in V(I), then c(t) lies in b⁻¹V(I). Otherwise choose z∈V(J) with b(z)=b(c(t)). Both z and c(t) lie over the complementary open of V(I). The restriction of b there is an isomorphism, hence injective on points, so z=c(t). This proves the reverse inclusion.
